newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Unemployment drops in Greater Buenos Aires.
newsitem.headline: Unemployment drops in Greater Buenos Aires.

text.p: Unemployment in Greater Buenos Aires fell in May to 17.3 percent from 18 percent last May and 18.8 percent in October last year, an Economy Ministry source said Monday.

The estimate was made after 80 percent of the results of the latest twice-yearly employment survey had been calculated. It does not indicate whether the improvement was due to an increase in jobs or to a drop in the number of people actively seeking employment, the official said.
The results of the job survey for the densely-populated district comprising the Argentine capital and surrounding industrial belt "are better than expected," the official said.

The Argentine government has forecast the final results of the job survey will show a nationwide drop in unemployment to 16.3 percent in May against 17.3 percent last October and 17.1 percent in May last year.

With mid-term elections in Congress looming in October, unemployment is the number one problem for Peronist President Carlos Menem, who has seen the jobless rate more than double from just seven percent when he first took power in 1989.
